title: CLR/40/2014 of Suresh Pal Vs Rajendra Prasad Kandwal

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
CIVIL REVISION NO. 40 OF 2014
Suresh Pal ............Revisionist.
Versus
Rajendra Prasad Kandwal ......Respondent.
Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the respondent.
Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 The building, in which the tenancy of the revisionist is
situate, is covered by the Act No. 13 of 1972. Accordingly,
revisionist is entitled to protections provided in the said Act. The
protection, provided in the said Act, is not applicable to such a tenant,
who has, amongst others, sublet the tenancy. In the event of non-payment of rent for two consecutive months also, protection of the
said Act is not available to the tenant of a building covered by the said
Act. In the suit, respondent / plaintiff alleged that there has been
default in payment of rent and, in addition thereto, defendant has
inducted a sub-tenant in the suit property. In the written statement,
while non-payment of rent consecutively for two months was denied,
it was contended that the tenancy was in favour of the revisionist as
well as in favour of the person, who was alleged by the plaintiff to be
the father of the sub-tenant of the revisionist. Therefore, in the written
statement, it was accepted by the revisionist that he is a tenant of the
tenancy in question and, in addition to him, he has a co-tenant. It was,
accordingly, his obligation to establish that such a co-tenancy was
created. In order to do so, revisionist purported to rely upon a
photostat copy of the alleged agreement dated 2nd February, 1984.
Photostat copies of a document are not even secondary evidence. No
Court, therefore, could look into such photostat copies as a piece of
evidence. Apart therefrom, revisionist failed to produce any evidence
to show that, in fact, he had a co-tenant in respect of the selfsame
tenancy. Revisionist, by taking the aforesaid plea in the written

2
statement, accepted the fact that the person, who has been alleged by
the plaintiff to be the sub-tenant, is in occupation of the tenancy on the
basis that his father is a co-tenant of the tenancy. Therefore, the plea
taken was the plea of confession and avoidance. Revisionist, having
had confessed and could not avoid the confession in the backdrop of
the evidence on record, accepted the fact that sub-tenancy has been
created. In those circumstances, revisionist could not retain the shop
even for one second after termination of the tenancy. There is no
scope of interference in the revision. The revision fails and the same
is dismissed.
(Barin Ghosh, C.J.)
27.05.2014
Rathour
